analysis: The 64-negative trial succeeded: host macro validation HR@10 increased from 0.5625 to 0.5737 (+0.0112 reported). Category HR@10 changed as follows: Movies_and_TV 0.595→0.625, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.615→0.595, Electronics 0.370→0.375, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.670→0.700. Gains in Movies and CDs outweighed the Industrial decline. Electronics remains below its original 0.420 baseline. This supports retaining broader uniform negative supervision as a promising setting, but one trial does not establish causality or consistency across seeds. No held-out performance was measured. Allocated GPU time was 468.15 seconds.
code_summary: Per-category SASRec + MultVAE ensemble. SASRec uses two causal attention blocks, 64-dimensional embeddings, and a gated causal prefix-mean preference branch. Training increases uniform negatives from 16 to 64 per active position, excludes the user's complete training history, allows duplicates, and applies 65-way positive-first cross-entropy. Active-position scoring avoids embedding padded negatives. MultVAE and its reconstruction/KL objective remain unchanged. Each member restores its best validation checkpoint; reciprocal-rank fusion uses constant 60 and selects among five SASRec weights using validation hits. All four dataset routes, trial-local artifacts, predictor writer, and checkpoint/predictor agreement checks are preserved. Added deterministic checks cover sampling, padding, loss agreement, and gradients while restoring RNG state.
